Went into A Fistful of Dollars expecting a tense western showdown and instead got 100 straight minutes of Clint Eastwood squinting at people like he’s trying to remember where he parked his horse. The pacing moves with all the urgency of a tumbleweed filing tax returns. Entire scenes consist of men silently staring at each other while a harmonica wheezes somewhere in the distance. By the time somebody finally got shot, I’d emotionally aged into a frontier grandparent. The storyline is somehow both incredibly simple and completely confusing. Two families hate each other, Clint wanders between them doing… something? Half the movie feels like arriving late to a barbecue where everyone already knows the gossip except you. Characters appear, glare ominously, then vanish forever like NPCs with unfinished dialogue trees. And emotional complexity? The deepest character development is “this guy looks sweaty and angry now.” Clint Eastwood’s character has roughly the emotional range of a granite countertop wearing a poncho. I’ve had more psychologically layered interactions with self checkout machines. Still, the soundtrack slaps. So congratulations to the trumpet guy for carrying the entire film on his back like a weary mule.

Filme violentamente marasmático em seu emaranhado de closes viris. Uma miscelânea de registros estilizados de tiros, torturas e rostos sujos de sangue e suor quase aderidos à película que nada me comunicam para além de uma construção redundante e artificial do poder "patriarcal" detido pelo personagem machão do Clint, sempre envolto por uma blindagem física e intelectual que o fortalece narrativamente sem dispor isso de modo funcional (ou, por que não dizer, interessante) na forma. Não poderia me entendiar, ou vaguear, menos com suas habilidades ostensivas com a pistola, ou com qualquer um dos porradeiros/tiroteios em objetivas/subjetivas – escolhas que pouco ressignificam a matéria.

At this point, I can confidently say that old westerns are my least favorite genre. The acting is never up to par for me and that holds true here, as well. Clint Eastwood is passable as the lead, but he feels too flat a lot of the time. There's no range or charisma. I recognize that that is part of the character he's playing, but I think he takes it too far. It's hard to tell if the supporting actors are awful or if it's just the TERRIBLE dubbing, which distracted me the entire movie. Dubbing seems nearly impossible to do well, or at the least, back in the Old Hollywood days. Every dubbed performance here feels so stiff. The energy never truly matches the scene itself. I don't really care that the mouths don't match the words perfectly, just that the performance doesn't match the physicality of what the actors are doing. On the positive side, the pacing and editing in this film are easily better than most other westerns I've seen, which all seem to drag out the runtime needlessly. This movie is 99 minutes long and there's zero extra fluff from what I can tell. The plot is interesting, even if its execution comes across as cheesy at times due to the writing and dubbed performances. The third act is surprisingly cool. I went in with tempered expectations and they were basically met. I'll stick around for the rest of the trilogy since The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly has such a great reputation, but I won't hold my breath. Old westerns just aren't my thing. 56/100

I get that this is a beloved classic for many people.  I am glad people have their things they like.  But this is another in a long line of movies that just don't hold up by today's standards.  The music is cool and iconic.  Some of the scenery is ok.  You can really see where some of the icons of the old western came from in this.  But ultimately, it is an ok story about a guy that keeps playing 2 gangs against each other.  Sure, it is someone fun here and there and it has been parodied countless times.  But it is really overacted and the sound and voice overs are pretty terrible.  The special effects are ridiculous.  Etc.  This does not exactly inspire me to run out and watch The Good The Bad and The Ugly or For Few Dollars More anytime soon.  And wow.  the brown face and blood make-up is awful in this.

A Fistful of Dollars est un film que je respecte davantage pour son importance historique que pour ses qualités. Je comprends parfaitement pourquoi il a marqué le western et popularisé le western spaghetti, notamment grâce au charisme de Clint Eastwood et à son concept simple mais efficace. Cependant, j'ai trouvé l'ensemble assez limité. L'intrigue est très basique, les personnages manquent de profondeur et le film ne m'a jamais réellement captivé. Certains éléments ont évidemment vieilli, mais même en tenant compte de son époque, je n'ai pas ressenti grand-chose devant le récit. Un film important dans l'histoire du cinéma, mais dont l'intérêt aujourd'hui me semble surtout historique plutôt que cinématographique.
